reason: At base, the object JIT fastpass leaks the swallowed issue's value (safeParse({}) returns {a:"leaked"}), so the parsed output has a key for the omitted property, contradicting the expected result.
After the fix the JIT branch drops values written alongside swallowed issues on absent keys, matching the jitless/async paths the test also checks, and present failing keys still report failure.
At base the paragraph continuation lookahead only treats spaces-only lines as blank, so a tab-only separator line is absorbed and the two lines are rendered as one paragraph instead of two.
The revised lookahead [ \t]+\n counts tab-only lines as blank, so the tab separator splits the text into two paragraph elements as the test expects.
The change only touches the request error-stack decoration path; a successful 200 JSON response is parsed by the untouched transformResponse, so data is a parsed object at base.
The PR affects only error-path stack decoration, not successful response parsing, so response data is still exposed as a parsed JSON object at head.
The PR only changes the negative-number exponent regex; boolean flag parsing is untouched, so '--verbose' still parses as true with no unknown-option error at base.
The change is confined to negative-number detection; boolean flag handling is unaffected, so the flag still parses to true at head.
At base JsonTreeReader.nextInt() lacks the ASCII check, so a JSON string of full-width digits is silently coerced to 123 instead of raising a parsing error as the test expects.
After the fix, nextInt/nextLong on a string token call validateAscii and throw MalformedJsonException for full-width digits, matching the expected error behavior.
At base the search_path regex only keeps [a-zA-Z0-9$] characters, so 'test-db' is split into 'test' and 'db' and the SQL quotes them separately instead of one 'test-db' schema.
The blocklist regex keeps hyphens and accented characters together, so 'test-db' is emitted as a single quoted schema name in the search path statement.
The PR only changes ByteBufferUtil.fromStream buffer recycling on exception; the image loading/transformation pipeline is untouched, so a configured center-crop is still applied.
Transformations are not affected by the ByteBufferUtil buffer-recycling change, so a center-crop configured on an ImageView request is still applied at head.
The PR only caches the allowedSymbols+alphanumerics union; the computed behavior at base is identical, so an identifier with an allowed extra symbol still passes the naming rule.
The cached set is refreshed in the initializer and when allowedSymbols is applied from configuration, preserving the equivalent union, so configured allowed symbols still suppress violations.
The PR is a compilation-only fix (adding <cstdint> for GCC 15) that does not touch image loading or data-URI decoding, so a percent-encoded SVG data URI still loads and draws.
The PR only adds Afrikaans week/weekdays translation strings; datetime shift/DST arithmetic is untouched, so the 10-hour shift across spring-forward still yields 05:30 -05:00.
The <cstdint> include is a compilation-only change with no runtime effect on image loading or data-URI handling, so the percent-encoded SVG still decodes and loads.
The PR only changes cookie-header parsing; the form-urlencoded content decoder is untouched, so an empty body with an all-optional type still decodes to all-nil without a 422.
Cookie parsing change does not affect content decoding, so empty-body form-urlencoded decode of the optional-only type still succeeds with a normal handler response.
The PR only fixes comment/variable spelling; the in-memory filesystem Remove behavior is unchanged, so removing a non-empty directory still errors and leaves contents intact.
Spelling-only changes do not affect filesystem semantics, so Remove on a non-empty directory still returns a not-empty error and leaves the directory and file in place.
The PR only adjusts a JSON encoding test; the schema Comparator logic is untouched, so comparing with two equally valid rename candidates completes without undefined-key warnings.
The json_encode flags change is confined to tests; schema comparison behavior is unchanged and completes without PHP warnings at head.
Locale translation additions do not affect timezone shift arithmetic, so shifting 10 hours across the US/Central spring-forward still yields 2025-03-09T05:30:00 -05:00.
The PR only changes CircuitBreakerStateMachine predicate evaluation; the semaphore RateLimiter refresh scheduling is untouched, so permits keep replenishing after changeLimitForPeriod.
The circuit-breaker predicate fix does not touch rate limiter code, so the scheduled refresh continues replenishing permits up to the lowered limit at head.

The no-var autofix rewrites var to let, which puts the variable in the temporal dead zone; foo() invoked before 'let a = 1' executes throws a ReferenceError instead of printing undefined, and the prefer-template PR doesn't touch no-var.

After autofix var count becomes let count, so printCount invoked via schedule() before the declaration line reads count while it is in the TDZ and throws a ReferenceError; the prefer-template ASI change does not alter no-var's rewrite.
The PR only changes logformatter_adapter message formatting; spider job-resume state, request queues, and sitemap scheduling are untouched, so a restart with the same JOBDIR resumes crawling.
Log-formatting changes do not affect the persistent job infrastructure, so the resumed sitemap spider keeps crawling additional pages before closing.

The sanitize bidi-control change does not involve wrapping or highlighting; the capacity-overflow handling for narrow terminal widths is already present at base (per the changelog), so bat exits 0 with the background clamped.
Wrapping and row-background rendering are untouched by the sanitize preprocessor change, so a wide character at terminal width 1 still renders without a capacity-overflow abort at head.
The PR only optimizes the RFC5424 syslog parser regex; the file output plugin's per-key buffering and symlink creation are untouched, so both aa and bb symlinks are created for the single batch.
Syslog parsing changes do not affect file-output symlink maintenance, so the follow-up record for a previously seen key still updates that key's symlink.
The PR changes only ConcurrentBag's virtual-thread yield spin; default pool-name generation uses a static counter and never locks the System properties object, so pool construction is not blocked.
ConcurrentBag spin behavior is unrelated to pool-name generation, which takes no lock on system properties, so concurrent pool creation without names completes without deadlock at head.
The PR only fixes SORT's ACL key parsing; RDB background save is untouched, so BGSAVE on a 32-bit server still completes successfully with rdb_last_bgsave_status:ok.
The sortGetKeys ACL fix does not affect persistence, so the automatic background save still starts and terminates successfully with a valid dump.rdb at head.
The PR only fixes window-local CWD bookkeeping in context switches; CTRL-A number increment code is untouched, so incrementing the 50-digit value preserves all digits at base.
The cwd/context fix does not involve operator arithmetic, so CTRL-X decrements the 50-digit number by exactly one without losing digits at head.
The PR only changes the external file cache; list concatenation type resolution is untouched, so [1] || NULL still yields a NULL value typed as INTEGER[].
The file-cache race fix does not affect function/type binding, so pipe and list_concat still both report an array type for the NULL list result at head.
The ScrollBar input-event change is unrelated to object lifetime; RefCounted still delivers NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE while the object is valid, so reading members in the handler works.
ScrollBar touch handling does not affect RefCounted lifecycle, so the PREDELETE notification still fires with readable members and no crash at head.
The PR only adds a DecisionTree categorical-feature error; f_regression is untouched and its long-standing behavior for constant columns returns F=0.0 with p=1.0 and no sqrt warning.
r_regression is not affected by the DecisionTree change; a near-constant column with nonzero variance yields a finite correlation inside [-1,1] without warnings at head.
The PR touches only the UI swagger component; Vault Agent's file sink still applies the configured octal mode, so the token file gets 0640 at base.
The swagger-ui change does not affect agent sink logic, so a 0600 file mode is still applied to the token file at head.

At base, write_usage with empty args does not render the usage prefix properly (the issue this PR fixes), so the first help line is blank or has a spurious trailing space rather than exactly 'Usage: cli'.
After the fix, write_usage with no args emits just 'Usage: cli' with the trailing separator stripped, so the first help line matches exactly.
The PR only fixes IPv6 host parsing in the dev server and test client; the default JSON provider still renders dict views with Content-Type application/json and compact separators at base.
Host/port parsing changes do not affect response serialization, so dict-returning views are still delivered as compact application/json at head.
The PR only changes deprecated-alias lookup in schema generation; required-field validation is core behavior and still raises a missing-field error at base.
The alias-lookup fix does not affect model field validation, so omitting a required field still fails with a validation error identifying it as missing at head.
logging.WARN is just an alias of logging.WARNING (value 30), so effective levels are identical; echo off still suppresses SQL info records and echo on still logs them at base.
The WARN-to-WARNING rename changes no numeric behavior, so default engine logging still suppresses routine SQL output with echo off and logs it with echo on.
After the first access triggers generation, both the real column and the aliased computed attribute are plain generated method reads, so the access-time ratio stays near 1x and far below 20x at base.

At head, method_missing now always calls define_attribute_methods, but once generated the alias and column reads are direct method calls, so steady-state access cost remains comparable and under the 20x bound.
At base, called listeners stay in the callStack across dispatches (only non-called ones are removed), so two dispatches with one listener yield two entries from getCalledListeners.
At head the new code deduplicates called listeners per event (in_array guard), so after dispatching twice the list contains a single entry, not one per invocation as the test requires.
The shellcheck fixes keep the generated completion logic equivalent; custom hooks still receive the subcommand being completed, so each sibling subcommand gets its own scoped suggestions at base.
The while-read replacement of COMPREPLY assignment preserves which completion function runs, so per-subcommand dynamic suggestions still come from the correct hook at head.
qs's default arrayLimit is 20, so 25 repeated keys parse into an object keyed by numeric index instead of an array, breaking the expected ['1'..'25'] result at base.
qs 6.14.0 raised the default arrayLimit above 20, so 25 repeated 'ids' values parse into a proper array preserving order at head.
At base get_environ_proxies takes only the URL argument and returns a proxy dict (possibly empty), so a single-argument call succeeds as expected.
At head get_environ_proxies gained a required no_proxy parameter with no default, so calling it with only a URL raises TypeError instead of returning a dict.
At base parse_unit_value returns None for words starting with '.', so '.foons' falls back to a plain string in the list literal, yielding '.foons' from get 0.
The fix lets '.' start a unit value but '.foons' has no digits to parse as a number, so it still falls back to a string and the list element reads '.foons'.
The PR exists to fix a failure when sending HEAD requests with an Accept-Encoding header via the cURL handler; at base the sink is still connected for HEAD, which was the reported fatal-error source.
After the fix, no sink or write function is attached for HEAD requests, so a HEAD with Accept-Encoding completes and returns a normal response without errors.
The PR only changes how maps are rendered inside list diffs; a plain match failure of :foo against %{bar: [1|2]} still produces the standard 'match (=) failed' error showing both values at base.
Map escaping in list diffs does not affect basic match-assertion diffs, so the assertion still fails cleanly with left and right values shown and no formatting crash at head.
At base the css_props block still runs teardown removing the style element, which breaks the CSS custom property on dynamic-component re-render — the exact bug this PR exists to fix.
After the PR, css_props no longer removes its element and the dynamic component is hydrated/mounted with css props intact, so the inner text stays red before and after the toggle.

At base the transform guard only checks code.includes('new URL') and 'import.meta.url', and the working regex uses \s* which spans newlines, so the multi-line new URL reference is rewritten and the asset is emitted.
The refactor adds a code filter /new\s+URL.+import\.meta\.url/ whose .+ cannot span newlines, so the multi-line new URL(...) reference is no longer matched and the asset is not emitted at head.
At base the preview child is launched without FZF_CURRENT_ITEM, so NUL bytes in the item never reach the child environment and the preview command runs and shows its output.
The PR exports FZF_CURRENT_ITEM holding the raw item text, which for NUL-delimited input embeds NUL bytes into the preview child's environment, causing the child process to fail to start.
At base, switching to edgeToEdge calls setSystemUiVisibility with only LAYOUT_* flags, which replaces and thereby clears the immersive hide flags, so the system bars reappear.

At head, entering edge-to-edge only calls WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(window,false), which on API 30+ does not clear the immersiveSticky hide flags still applied to the decor view, so the bars stay hidden.
At base the parser has no multiple-assignment check for case patterns, so ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes) is accepted without any syntax error.

The new visitor inserts keyword names (keyword.attr) as bindings, so ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes) reports a spurious 'multiple assignments to name `num_classes` in pattern' syntax error in preview mode.
At base the value-slice branch indexes sli.Index(i) without growing the slice, so decoding two blocks into a one-entry pre-populated list panics with a slice index out of range error.
The fix appends a fresh zero value when the block index is past the slice length, so both blocks decode in order, overwriting the placeholder and yielding exactly two entries.
At base the mock keeps the instance's own timezone when no timezone is pinned, so Carbon::now() formats the mocked moment in America/Los_Angeles instead of the UTC default.
The fix converts the mocked instance to the passed timezone or the application default when reading it back, so Carbon::now() renders the moment in UTC as expected.
The old regex /^[\/\\]{2}[^/\\]+/ only matches exactly two leading slash characters, so '///test.com', '/\t//test.com' and '/\/test.com' are all classified as not protocol-relative.
The new regex /^([/\\]\s*){2,}[^/\\]/ accepts three slashes, slashes separated by whitespace, and mixed slash/backslash prefixes, so all three strings are classified as protocol-relative.
The PR only swaps an internal byte-array accessor inside the hash-combining helpers; the MD5 implementation is untouched, so md5('abc') still yields the standard digest at base.
getBytesInternal returns the same bytes as asBytes for plain hash codes, so the combining helpers still produce identical digests and MD5('abc') is unchanged at head.
At base the generator emits the client for a method with a valid GET attribute and issues the GET request as usual; nothing in the workflow is affected.
The PR is a pure refactor moving diagnostics to a dedicated class with unchanged codes, messages and severities, so source generation and the resulting GET request are identical.
The removed continue statements were the final statement of each loop branch, so control flow is unchanged and a plain HTTP/1.1 GET still returns 200 with the exact body at base.
Dropping the redundant continues keeps the loop semantics identical (the h2 upgrade reader's continue is replaced by an empty block), so the fresh HTTP/1.1 request still completes with the full body.
At base to_iso8601/2 drops the format after converting to the ISO calendar and delegates to to_iso8601/1, so a :basic request on a non-ISO-calendar date silently returns the extended form.
The fix forwards the requested format into the converted date, so a Holocene-calendar date formatted with :basic correctly yields the compact '20010101' representation.
At base setEndDate updates the internal end-date state but on PHP 8.2+ the native DatePeriod end property stays at the value from construction, so reading ->end returns the stale 2024-09-30.
The fix re-initializes the underlying DatePeriod after the end date is updated, so both the ->end property and getEndDate() report 2025-06-15 00:00:00.
At base the request headline is built from the normalized URI without any whitespace check, so a path containing a newline gets transmitted in the request line instead of raising.
The headline builder now raises RequestError 'Invalid request URI' when the resolved request URI contains whitespace, so the client refuses to transmit the newline-containing path.
The PR only modifies the Albanian sq.yml locale data; the default English number-to-words output for 1,000,000 and 2,000,000 is unchanged at base.
Adding a plural name to the Albanian million scale has no effect on English, so the conversions still return 'one million' and 'two million' at head.
The PR only changes property loading; singleton component resolution is untouched, so both resolutions return the same instance at base.
Filtering non-String property keys does not alter the module/component resolution path, so singleton scope still returns the identical instance on the second resolution.
At base the append/swap/remove implementation yields ('a',1),('z',2),('c',3) with order preserved, and the duplicate-key precondition still fires on the second replace.
The shared primitive performs the identical append/swap/remove (and the duplicate-key precondition is unchanged), so the replace result and the duplicate-key failure are the same at head.
At base the manual negative-clamp converts '-5MB' to 0 bytes before multiplying, so the accessor returns 0 as expected.
max(cast.ToInt(sizeStr), 0) is behaviorally identical to the manual clamp, so an invalid negative size still yields 0 bytes at head.

At base, with both a static and a wildcard child, findCaseInsensitivePathRec grabs children[0] (a static node) when wildChild is true, panicking with 'invalid node type' on the mis-cased and unmatched requests.
The fix tries static children via indices first and then the wildcard child at the end of the array, so /PREFIX/XXX redirects to /prefix/xxx and /prefix/a/b/c gets an ordinary not-found.
At base toBigInt returns the nil Int unchanged when Exp is 0, so Int64Value dereferences nil and panics on a valid Numeric with no digits.
toBigInt now returns a zero big.Int when Int is nil, so Int64Value returns 0 like Float64Value without any runtime error.
The PR only changes tab-stop handling in the renderer; calling Quit from another goroutine still stops the run loop promptly at base.
Restoring tab stops in flush/reset does not touch the run loop or quit path, so the program still exits without hanging or errors at head.
At base run_until_cancelled polls the wrapped future before consulting cancellation state, so the already-cancelled case still starts the operation and the guard panic is raised.
The fix checks is_cancelled() before building the runnable future, returning None immediately so the wrapped operation is never polled and no panic occurs.
The PR only skips loading ignore files in unreachable directories; case-insensitive matching behavior is untouched, so all letter cases still match at base.
Avoiding ignore-file loading at max depth does not alter pattern matching, so case-insensitive search still reports every occurrence regardless of case at head.
At base, without a container default, a skip_deserializing field is replaced with Default::default() when the input omits it, so the field gets its zero value.
The refactored condition (container_default.is_none()) is equivalent to the old Default::None check for the no-container-default case, so the skipped field still initializes to its default value.
